Commentary.Commentary: None of the visitors' batsmen could cash in as they all went for the ugly shots. Just wanted to swing around and that led to their downfall. If it wasn't for Powell's cameo later on, the Caribbeans could have faced even more embarrassment. Plunkett stole the show with the ball while Rashid too did well to stop the leakage. Others were running for shelter at the start but did well at the death. So, the target looks well under the sight for the hosts who have a deep batting line-up. But can they chase it down or will we see some inspiring bowling from West Indies? Join us in a bit to find out...

106/1 after first 10 overs swells to just 176/9 in the next 10, says Nasser Hussain on air! What-a-comeback-from-England! After being put into bat, the Windies' openers came out with a mindset which was to dispatch anything and everything that's in the arc. Gayle started the riot and soon Lewis joined hands. Together they racked up over 70 in the Powerplay to set the tone. However, a lazy run out followed by a couple of quick wickets from Plunkett dented all the momentum the tourists had.
Almost a yorker on middle, dug out towards Morgan at extra cover for a single. WEST INDIES FINISH ON 176/9!
Very full on middle, driven to long on for a run. This brings up 175 for the Windies.

SIX! Bang! Finally Nurse connects one! Full on middle and off, Ashley clears his front leg and clobbers it over mid on. It goes high in the air but has it got the distance? Yes, it has as the long on fielder watches it go above his head and over the fence.
Sprayed full and wide outside off, Williams squeeze it towards third man for a single.
Kesrick Williams is the last man in.

OUT! Plumb! Taylor is hurt as well! A length delivery around off, angling into the batsman. Taylor clears his front leg and swings his bat across. The ball doesn't bounce much and hits Jerome on the back leg. Hits him on the thigh and he immediately catches it in pain. However, Jordan appeals for lbw and it's given by the umpire. So three dot balls on the trot after the resumption.
Full toss outside off, Taylor covers the stumps and carves it towards Roy at point. The English opener fumbles a touch but doesn't concede a run. Jerome has missed out on this one!
Curran bowls it slow and full on middle and off, Nurse displays a text-book forward defence.
We are back! We are all set but for an exciting finish? Let's wait and find out. Here comes Tom Curran to bowl the last ball of the penultimate over...
Update 2010 local - It was just a passing shower and it has gone away now. The groundsmen are out doing their best.  It seems that if there's no more rain, the MATCH WILL RESUME AT 2020 LOCAL.

It's absolutely bucketing down at the moment. The umpires after doing their best to complete the innings run out of patience and decide the rain is more than enough to take the players off now. They call in for the covers. The umbrellas are up in the stands, the DJ is playing some good songs and it's good to see the English crowd enjoying themselves out there. Let's hope it clears out soon and we get back in...
Fullish delivery around middle and off, driven to long on for a single.
Nurse heaves it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Jerome Taylor walks in next.

OUT! Powell is the latest victim! He was trying to up the ante for his team and holes out in the process. Length delivery, angling into the batsman, Rovman clears his front leg and looks to heave it across. Gets a top edge and the ball goes high in the air. Jordan at deep mid-wicket, keeps his eyes on the ball, gets underneath it and manages to hang on to a great catch in the rain. He is relieved after catching that and the smiles are back on the Englishmen's faces seeing Powell's back.

SIX! That's lost in the night sky! High full toss on middle, Powell clears his front leg bang he goes. Pulls with authority over square leg and the ball sails into the stands. All eyes are on the square leg umpire, who signals nothing. The replay shows that it was a marginal call.

DROPPED! It was a difficult chance but Plunkett had done the hard work! Full on middle and off, Nurse lofts it stylishly over mid off. Liam in the deep, sprints ahead, dives in front, gets both his hands behind it but the wet ball spills out. One can feel for Plunkett here as it was a difficult chance, rain was in the air and the ball was wet as well. Nurse gets a life and a single as well.
The rain is getting slightly heavier now.
Nurse drills it down to long on. Wants two but won't get it.
Very full around off, Ashley crouches, makes some room and jams it out towards cover.

An appeal for an LBW! On a length and coming back in, Powell looks to clip it away but gets it off something towards the off side. Jordan puts in an appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Seemed like a leg bye but the umpire signals it as a run.
SIX! He's picked the bones out of that one! Slower delivery, Powell reads it and does so early. Waits on the back foot and absolutely murders it over the cow corner for half a dozen.
Good ball! Almost a yorker, wide outside off, Rovman looks to dig it out. The ball goes through to Buttler.
A slight drizzle in the air.
Wide! Slower ball but it's miles down the leg side. Powell looks to swing at it but fails to get any wood on it. 150 up for the Windies!
A bit ahead of a length outside off, swatted off the inner half to deep square leg for a single.
Wide! Short and angling down leg, Nurse moves inside the line and makes an easy leave.
Short delivery, sits up nicely for Nurse, who pulls it hard. Unfortunately, finds the man at deep square leg for a single.
Driven through mid on for a single.
Easy knock down the ground for a single.
OUCH! Curran surprises Nurse with a sharp bumper. Nurse goes for the pull but gets an outside edge onto the helmet. This will shake him up.
Wide! Angling down leg, Nurse looks to flick it away but misses. A wide is signalled.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Nurse feels for it but gets beaten.
Length delivery, angling in, worked on the leg side for a single.
Change in bowling too. Tom Curran is back into the attack.
Ashley Nurse walks in next!

OUT! Adil Rashid too picks up a 3-fer! Tossed up on middle, Narine like his skipper, kneels down to sweep. He however doesn't get across but misses and gets rapped on the pads. Rashid appeals and up goes the finger straightaway. The leggie is delighted as he ends up with the figures of 4-0-25-3!
Full outside off, pushed in the cover region. Morgan there half stops and concedes a single.
Served around off, spinning away, Narine prods ahead and looks to clip it away but the ball takes outer half and rolls on the off side. Another single is taken.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot to long on. One run added to the total.
Leading edge! Tossed up around leg, spinning away, Narine looks to turn it away but gets a leading edge. The ball lobs towards mid off for a single.
Sunil Narine strides out to bat next!

OUT! Timber! Around the legs! Tossed up on middle, spinning away. Brathwaite kneels down a long way across to sweep but misses. The ball goes on to hit the middle pole. This is a dismal period for the Men from the Caribbean and now their skipper is also back in the hut. Can they find a way back?
10 from the 15th over! The batsman runs it down to third man towards Rashid to keep strike.
Slower ball, served outside off, worked away through square leg for a single.
Back of a length outside off, Carlos stands tall and dabs it in front of point for one.
Fuller and slower in pace, dipping in, clipped in front of square leg for a single.
FOUR! Edged and away! Short of a length delivery outside off, Powell throws his hands at it. Once again gets an outside edge and it races down towards the third man fence for a boundary.
Length ball outside off, Powell looks to drive it through the line but gets it off the outer part down to third man for a couple.
Chris Jordan is called back into the attack.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Worked away down the leg side for a single.
Carlos Brathwaite, the skipper is the new man in.

OUT! Now, Rashid strikes! West Indies are losing the plot here. Adil bowls a short delivery around off, spinning away, Walton hangs back and goes for the pull. The ball deserves to be hit but Chadwick doesn't get it off the meat. The ball skies towards deep mid-wicket, where Willey, runs to his right and takes a good sliding catch with his fingers pointing skywards. The visitors have lost half their side now. England have picked up 5 wickets for 50 runs, great stuff from the home side!
Wrong one around middle and off, punched off the back foot to long on for a single.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
In the air... but safe! Short delivery from Walton, who tries to pull it away but gets it off the toe end. It fall safely in the deep mid-wicket region. A single is taken.
The batsman plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. The batsmen have run through for a single. Plunkett finishes with figures of - 4-0-27-3!
Angling into the batsman, eased down to long on for a single.
A touch ahead of a length around off, tapped back to the bowler.
Fullish around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Rovman Powell is the new batsman in!

OUT! 3-fer for Plunkett! Short delivery does the trick for him. He has been using this ball to choke the Windies for runs and now he gets the prized wicket of Pollard. Banged in short, angling into the batsman. It gets big on Kieron, who goes through with his pull shot. Catches the top edge and the ball flies towards fine leg. Curran the man there, positions himself perfectly and stays calm to complete the catch with a reverse cup. England are chipping away at the wickets and that will keep the visitors in check.
Slower delivery from Plunkett, worked behind square on the leg side for a single.
Tossed up outside off, Pollard pushes it on the off side.
Flatter delivery around off, Pollard chops it besides the track and it goes on the bounce to the keeper.
A touch shortish around off, spinning in, Walton checks his shot and the ball runs down to long on. Another single is taken.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.
FOUR! A gentle tickle! Sliding down leg, Pollard gets across and just clips it round the corner. The ball runs away to the fine leg fence for another boundary.
Wrong 'un from Rashid. Pollard fails to read it and is rapped on the pads as he looks to defend off the front foot.
Adil Rashid is back on!
Short and angling into Pollard. The West Indian looks to turn it on the leg side but is early to close his bat face. Gets a leading edge on the off side and a single is taken.

What happened there? Plunkett comes steaming in and all of a sudden Pollard pulls out at the last moment. Not sure what distracted him. He apologies as the poor bowler will have to run again to deliver.
Kieron Pollard is the new man in.

OUT! Samuels holes out! Clever stuff from Plunkett. He follows Samuels with a length delivery, who is backing away to make room. Marlon gets cramped for room and just swings his bat across. Gets it off the splice and the ball lobs to Root at mid-wicket. Double strike from Plunkett and he has got the hosts back into the game.
Back of a length delivery outside off, run down to third man for a single.
SIX! Walton joins the party straightaway! Plunkett pitches it on a length around off, Walton clears his front leg and absolutely murders it, hitting it miles into the stands behind long on.
Plunkett welcomes Walton with a short ball, angling into him. Chadwick is ready and pulls it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Chadwick Walton is the next man in! A slip in place for him.

OUT! Lewis departs! Plunkett is the man who strikes for the hosts! He bowls it full around middle and off, Lewis makes room trying to smash it over mid off. Gets the power behind it but fails to get the elevation. It goes straight to Root in the circle and he doesn't drop it. The home side is delighted and why won't they be! It's a big, big wicket! The dangerous West Indian has to make the long walk back. Will this bring the run-rate in control?
Lewis goes back and punches it down the ground to long off for a single.
Wide! Darts it down the leg side, Lewis fails to flick it away. Second wide of the over.
Slower through the air on middle and off, spinning in, worked with soft hands on the leg side for a single.

2nd T20I FIFTY FOR EVIN LEWIS! Sliding into the batsman, Lewis clips it in front of square on the leg side and runs across for a single. Gets to his half century in just 26 balls. What a knock it has been from him, thoroughly entertaining!
The batsman drives this through the covers. One run added to the total.
Another straighter one on middle and leg, eased down to long on for a single.
Wide! Once again Root darts it into the batsman, who shuffles and goes for a pull but misses. A wide is signalled.
Sliding into the pads, Lewis looks to work it away but misses and the ball brushes the pads.
Joe Root is back on.
Fullish on the pads, clipped nicely towards deep square leg for a single.
Angling in from a length around middle, tucked away towards mid-wicket for one.
FOUR! Slapped away! Length delivery outside off, some width on offer as well. Samules makes room and thwacks it away through point to find the fence.
Angles in a length delivery on middle, Samuels looks to pull but the ball bounces off the deck and he gets an inside edge on the pads.
Back of a length outside off, tapped off the back foot towards point.
Bangs in a short delivery, angling in, Marlon is quick to duck under it.
SIX! Lewis won't hold back! Tossed up around off, Lewis lofts it and does so cleanly to clear the long off fence for a maximum to end the over.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single.

An appeal for LBW! Tossed up around leg, Evin gets down to sweep it away but gets it off the pads. Adil Rashid continues to appeal but the umpire shakes his head. It was clearly pitching outside leg. A leg bye taken.
FOUR! Up and over! Sees the loop, sees the flight and Lewis is ready to cash in. Takes his front foot out of the away and goes bang over extra cover for a one bounce boundary.
Loopy delivery outside off, Marlon looks to drive it but gets an inside edge on the pads as the ball rolls away towards cover for a single.
Floats it up around off, Samuels drives it back to the leggie.
Adil Rashid comes into the attack now. Bumble on air says not great weather for leg spinners!
Length ball on the pads, tucked behind square on the leg side for a single to keep strike.
Wide! Strays this one down the leg side, Marlon looks to work it away but seems to have missed it. Buttler collects it to his left and appeals but it's signaled as a wide.
Shorter in length outside off, Samuels shoulders his arms to that one.
Fuller ball on middle and leg, whipped through mid-wicket for a single.
Marlon Samuels is the new man in.

OUT! Run Out! England get the breakthrough! But to be honest, it was really a lazy effort from Gayle. Back of a length around off, Gayle with an angled bat dabs it towards Roy at backward point. He sets off rather slowly and is guilty of ball-watching. The English opener is quick to throw the ball at the bowler's end and Liam takes the bails off. They refer it upstairs and replays show Gayle is just short of his crease. The hosts needed to put an end to this partnership and they have done just that.
A run out appeal against Gayle is taken upstairs. Seems like the big man is struggling. He didn't even drag his bat in nor did he dive...
Short of a length outside off, slapped towards sweeper cover for a single.
FOUR! Runs continue to come! Plunkett from over the wicket, hurls it down the leg side. It's all too easy for Lewis who just clips it fine off his pads and the ball races away towards the fence.
Liam Plunkett is brought into the attack now. Can he provide the breakthrough?

A rare dot to end the over and the Powerplay! This time Curran surprises Gayle with a bouncer. Chris ducks under it and lets it through to the keeper. 72/0 at the end of Powerplay. England have been absolutely hammered all over the place in this phase.

Back of a length delivery, angling across. Lewis stands tall and pulls it flat over mid-wicket. Bairstow in the deep, runs to his left, gets to the ball and pushes the ball back in. A single is taken!
Good delivery, this! Curran surprises Lewis with a well-directed bouncer. Evin gets in an awkward positions and mistimes his pull towards short fine leg.

SIX! It's raining sixes at Chester-le-Street! Again it's full around leg, Evin Lewis gets across and whips it over mid-wicket. Bairstow in the deep tries to get under it but the ball sails over him for a maximum.
FOUR! Easy-peasy for Lewis! Fuller on the pads, Lewis shuffles a touch and flicks it cleanly over backward square leg. Finds the gap and the fence as well. A boundary is signalled!

SIX! Carnage in the middle! A touch ahead of a length around off, Lewis clears his front leg and tonks it straight down the ground. Doesn't connect it off the middle but still manages to get the distance. Lewis into the act now!
SIX! Boom! No stopping, Gayle! Gets a length ball, makes some room and bashes it high and handsomely over extra cover for a biggie.
On the pads, Gayle looks to flick it away but fails to get any bat on it.
FOUR! Beautifully bowled! Length delivery on off, Gayle lofts it over mid off and a boundary results.
Shorter in length on middle, swatted away in front of square on the leg side for a single.
FOUR! Easily done! Full toss, wide outside off and slower in pace. Lewis throws his hand at it and gets it over extra cover for a boundary.
Fuller in length on middle and leg, it's drilled down to long on for just a single.
Another change in bowling as Chris Jordan comes on to bowl!

FOUR! Lewis gets into the groove now! Tom bowls it short on middle, Lewis pulls it firmly through mid-wicket. Hales in the deep dives to stop it but fails to do so cleanly. 15 runs from Curran's first over!
Fuller ball on the pads, worked away towards square leg for a single.

FOUR! Good shot! Short of a length delivery, it keeps rising off the deck. Gayle stays leg side and initially decides to pull but then resists and slaps it over the point region. The outfield isn't that quick but still will get a boundary. He's looking in some mood tonight!
Slower one on middle and off, Gayle goes back and defends it towards point.
Third man comes up!
SIX! Curran gets the treatment! Pitches it on a length on middle, Chris Gayle backs away a bit and belts it straight back down the ground for a huge biggie.
Length delivery, slanting away a touch, pushed into the off side.
Tom Curran replaces Root, who had a decent first over. He has a slip in place. Bowling to Gayle will surely be a stern test for the youngster!
Full toss on the pads, whipped towards long on for a single. 13 off the over!
Very full on the stumps, driven straight to mid off.
SIX! Downtown! Willey don't even look back, that's gone the distance! Fuller in length, right in the slot and Gayle smashes it down the ground for back-to-back maximums.

SIX! 100th T20I biggie for Christopher Henry Gayle! And he's nailed this one to achieve this milestone! It's a touch short, angling in, Gayle swivels a bit and pulls it off the meat of the bat to send it over the deep mid-wicket fence for a maximum.
Back of a length, coming back in on middle, Chris punches it towards the leg side.
On a length and around off, Gayle comes forward to defend.
Around off, it's defended gently off the front foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! That's a good shot! Root slows it through the air around off, Evin smashes it over extra cover for a boundary.
Looks to defend it off the back foot but gets an inside edge towards short fine leg.
Fuller and quicker through the air around off, jammed out towards the off side.
Starts off with a quicker one around middle, punched off the back foot towards cover.
That's strange! Joe Root to bowl from the other end. My colleague reminds me that he removed Gayle in the T20I World Cup finals so maybe, it must be the reason.
Outside off, the batsman leaves it alone.
Angling in from around middle, tucked in front of square on the leg side for a single.
Fuller and around off, pushed off the front foot towards mid off.
Wide! Fuller and way down the leg side, Lewis leaves it alone. Buttler dives full length to his right to stop that one.
Fuller and spearing in on the pads, Gayle flicks it through mid-wicket to get towards the other end.
On a good length around middle and off, defended by prodding forward a touch.
Two slips in place now...

FOUR! Edgyyyy! Willey from over the wicket, drops it on a length around middle and it shapes away a touch to square Gayle up. An outside edge is induced which evades the first slip and races away towards the third man fence for a boundary. The visitors are away!

It's time to get underway. The crowd have come in numbers to watch these two sides lock horns. They are waiting in anticipation. The fielding side and the umpires have made their out to the middle now. Now, out walk the Windies openers - Evin Lewis and Chris Gayle. England to begin with David Willey first up with just a slip in place. Let's roll...
WINDIES XI - Chris Gayle, Evin Lewis, Marlon Samuels, Chadwick Walton(w), Kieron Pollard, Rovman Powell, Carlos Brathwaite(c), Sunil Narine, Ashley Nurse, Jerome Taylor, Kesrick Williams.
ENGLAND XI - Jason Roy, Alex Hales, Joe Root, Eoin Morgan(c), Jonny Bairstow, Jos Buttler(w), Adil Rashid, David Willey, Liam Plunkett, Chris Jordan, Tom Curran.
TOSS - ENGLAND WIN THE TOSS AND OPT TO FIELD!

England will be high on confidence with their good show in the longest format but this time around they would look to take revenge. Ben Stokes and Moeen Ali have been rested but they still have enough firepower in the ranks to tussle the tourists. Who will come out on top? Stay with us as the toss is coming up shortly...

Hello and a warm welcome for the one-off T20I between the World Champs, the Windies and England. The last time these two met in a T20I encounter, it was in Kolkata in 2016 where the visitors pulled off a historic win to take the coveted cup. The Men from the Caribbean will hope for a similar performance today. What will draw attention is that they were really competitive in the recently concluded Test series although they were at the receiving end. With the big guns back in the side, expect them blast out today.
